question:
Students analyse the function $g(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x-2}\right)$. The inner rational expression is undefined at $x=2$ and never equals $0$. For $x>2$ it is positive, while for $x<2$ it is negative. As $x$ approaches $2$ from either side, the magnitude of the argument becomes increasingly large; as the magnitude of $x$ increases, the argument approaches $0$. These observations allow the students to determine the domain, exact range, sign, missing intercepts, and two-branch structure of the graph using only inverse-tangent properties.

(a) Determine the domain of $g$.

(b) Determine the exact range of $g$.

(c) Find the $y$-intercept and determine whether an $x$-intercept exists.

(d) Describe the limiting behaviour near $x=2$ and for increasingly large positive or negative $x$.
explanation:
(a)
The denominator $x-2$ cannot equal $0$. Therefore,
$$x\neq2$$
Hence, the domain is
$$(-\infty,2)\cup(2,\infty)$$

(b)
The quantity $\dfrac{1}{x-2}$ can assume every non-zero real value but can never equal $0$. Since $\tan^{-1}t$ has range $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and equals $0$ only when $t=0$,
$$\text{Range}=\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$

(c)
For the $y$-intercept, put $x=0$:
$$g(0)=\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$$
Thus, the $y$-intercept is $\left(0,-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$. An $x$-intercept would require
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x-2}\right)=0$$
which would require $\dfrac{1}{x-2}=0$. This is impossible, so no $x$-intercept exists.

(d)
As $x$ approaches $2$ from the right, $\dfrac{1}{x-2}$ becomes increasingly large and positive, so $g(x)$ approaches $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. As $x$ approaches $2$ from the left, the argument becomes increasingly large and negative, so $g(x)$ approaches $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. For increasingly large positive $x$, $g(x)$ approaches $0$ through positive values. For increasingly large negative $x$, it approaches $0$ through negative values. None of these limiting range-boundary values is attained.

options.A:
(a) Domain: $\mathbb{R}$

(b) Range: $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

(c) $y$-intercept: $\left(0,\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$; $x$-intercept: $(2,0)$

(d) $g(x)$ attains $\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ at $x=2$ and approaches $0$ as $x\to\pm\infty$
options.B:
(a) Domain: $(-\infty,2)\cup(2,\infty)$

(b) Range: $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

(c) $y$-intercept: $\left(0,-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$; no $x$-intercept

(d) $g(x)\to-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ as $x\to2^{-}$, $g(x)\to\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ as $x\to2^{+}$, and $g(x)\to0$ as $x\to\pm\infty$
options.D:
(a) Domain: $(2,\infty)$

(b) Range: $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

(c) No coordinate-axis intercepts

(d) $g(x)\to\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ as $x\to2^{+}$ and $g(x)\to0$ through positive values as $x\to\infty$
